title: Prophets not an ass’s shadow; factions charge (chs. 1–20)
english: Ambrose’s charge continues: Celsus’s True Word is answered. Prophetic place, birth, and passion of Christ are not idle shadows. Celsus mocks Christian factions; Origen notes philosophy also splits yet seeks truth.
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 2–3 Perseus TEI; no Chadwick/ANF Crombie.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B; condensed book CLOSEOUT.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Aristeas and pagan hero-tales vs the Gospel (chs. 21–40)
english: Celsus’s wonder-tales (Aristeas and the like) do not bind Christians; if he recounts them without belief, they prove nothing against Jesus’ history.
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 2–3 Perseus TEI; no Chadwick/ANF Crombie.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B; condensed book CLOSEOUT.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Teaching all — youths, slaves, the simple (chs. 41–60)
english: We confess we want to educate all with God’s word — youths and household servants included — against Celsus’s sneer that we hunt only the uneducated.

title: Soul’s immortality — BOOK III CLOSEOUT (chs. 61–81)
english: Citing philosophers on the soul’s immortality is fair polemic, not betrayal of the Christian word. Book III closes on that defense.
